newsitem.title: USA: Kmart says sees markdowns in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Kmart says sees markdowns in Q2.

text.p: Kmart Corp said Tuesday it expected to take markdowns in its fiscal second quarter to help clear out $100 million in extra inventory, mostly in womens' and mens' apparel.
Kmart finished its fiscal first quarter with a $600 million increase in inventory, a 9.0-percent rise from the year-ago period.

Kmart chairman Floyd Hall said half of that was due to improving sales, while the remaining amount was due to such things as product buildup for new stores and the forthcoming expansion of the Martha Stewart line.
"We think we can manage our way out of that," Hall told reporters following the retailer's annual meeting here. But he added: "We do have some markdown liability there."

During the meeting, Hall fielded several questions about when Kmart might reinstate its quarterly dividend. Hall said the company's board revisits the dividend policy on a frequent basis, but did not offer any specifics as to when the dividend might be reinstated.
Hall said the dividend issue depends on cash flow, and the money that would go toward a dividend is now being reinvested in other parts of the business.
"As soon as reasonably possible, we will reinstate the dividend," Hall said.
Kmart discontinued its $0.12 per share quarterly dividend in December 1995.
Kmart officials said they would look into allegations that Kmart purchased 73 tons of raincoats and ponchos from a company controlled by Chinese military officers.
Kmart spokeswoman Shawn Kahle said the company stands by its human rights policies as they relate to suppliers.
